chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan, Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Senani, al-Hussein ibn Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Mokattib, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Var'aq (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Abul-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan reported from Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, who said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to us from his father, from his grandfather, from his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, from his father, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them). And Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein ibn Zayd narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, from his father al-Hussein, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Ali! Give glad tidings to your followers and helpers of ten characteristics: The first is their good birth, the second is their good faith in God, the third is God's love for them, the fourth is spaciousness in their graves, the fifth is light on the Bridge between their eyes, the sixth is the removal of poverty from their sight and the enrichment of their hearts, the seventh is God's animosity towards their enemies, the eighth is safety from leprosy, vitiligo, and insanity, O Ali! The ninth is the shedding of sins and evil deeds from them, and the tenth is that they are with me in Paradise and I am with them.'

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge over Hell on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What are the ten characteristics promised to the followers of Ali (AS) in this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq narrates this hadith through multiple chains, emphasizing the high status of the *Shi'a* through ten distinct blessings ranging from spiritual purity to physical immunity from diseases like leprosy and madness. This tradition underscores the Shia belief in the special divine favor granted to the followers of Ahl al-Bayt, linking their earthly conduct with eternal reward and proximity to the Prophet. The mention of 'ease in the grave' and 'light on the Sirat' connects directly to core eschatological concepts in Shia theology regarding the intermediate state (*Barzakh*) and judgment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-10 The following tradition has been reported by Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qattan, Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Senani, al-Hussein ibn Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Mokattib and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Var’raq - may God be pleased with them - who narrated that Abul-Ab’bas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qat’tan quoted on the authority of Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zakariya, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zah’hak, on the authority of Zayd ibn Musa ibn Ja’far, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein (MGB) , on the authority of his father (MGB) , on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) . It was also narrated by Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of Sa’ed ibn Abdul Rahman al-Makhzoomi, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (MGB), on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (MGB), on the authority of his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB)

that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “O Ali! Give glad tidings of ten characteristics to your helpers and followers: The first is their being born legitimately. The second is their good belief in God. The third is the Honorable the Exalted God’s love for them. The fourth is the ease and comfort in their grave. The fifth is a bright light illuminating their path when they want to cross the Bridge . The sixth is the elimination of poverty from their sight and the enrichment of their hearts. The seventh is God’s animosity towards their enemies. The eight is that they will be immune from leprosy (plus vitiligo and insanity). O Ali! The ninth is that sins and wickedness will be shed from them. The tenth is that they shall be with me in Paradise, and I shall be with them.”
